newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex says sold crude contracts to U.S. refineries.
newsitem.headline: Pemex says sold crude contracts to U.S. refineries.

text.p: State oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) chairman Adrian Lajous said on Tuesday that Pemex has sold crude contracts to U.S. west coast refineries that previously had processed crude from Alaska.

"We are looking for new markets for our crude products...We have already concluded some specific transactions to place crude in the west coast of the United States with refineries that were using crude from Alaska," Lajous told reporters.
Lajous said that as Alaska's crude output falls, Pemex expects to tap the west coast market to make up the gap.
Pemex traders have said the oil giant has been looking to diversify crude exports and had specifically targeted west coast refineries.
Pemex was pushed to look for new markets as competition has increased from other Latin American producers, especially Venezuela, which has increased its production in line with Mexico.
On June 5, Pemex will inaugurate a $600 million refinery in Tula to specifically process heavy crude and fuel oil, Lajous said.
